The melting points of the given elements are approximately:

B. Nb (Niobium): ~2477°C
C. Re (Rhenium): ~3186°C
D. W (Tungsten): ~3422°C

Based on these values, tungsten (W) has the highest melting point among the given options. Tungsten is actually known for having the highest melting point of all metals and the second highest melting point of all elements (after carbon in its diamond form).

However, there's an important distinction to make: Carbon in its graphite form has a melting point of about 3550°C, while tungsten's melting point is about 3422°C. But carbon doesn't actually melt at atmospheric pressure - it sublimates (goes directly from solid to gas). Tungsten is the element with the highest true melting point.
